# R2ffac818b0: Spiral activations and coupled-Adam evidence audit (1ca756a4c129f87cf61f647e42436f7736ec9775)
# Spiral activations and coupled-Adam evidence audit
## Scope and provenance
Observations are pinned to `J50bc0cf08c29_research_e0001`. Inputs are 863 history records, refreshed KB claims and allowed lab measurements. `q_fa7235` comes from ranking_v3/epoch1; `q_fb4a7f` from dataflip500/epoch1. Lab results report held-out cross-entropy (CE), lower is better, as mean and standard deviation over ten seeds. Candidate ratios are computed only within the same set.
This report validates scoped observations, not a general activation or decay theory. An initial report was published before experiments; this version includes counterexamples and accepted KB changes.
## Reproduction of q_fa7235
For 2–3-turn spirals, T256 and shared RMSprop learning rate, the stated statistics reproduce: at lr≥1e-3, smooth GELU/SiLU candidates win 5/5 comparisons across three sets, median smooth/rectifier CE ratio **0.800109**. At lr≤3e-4, they win 3/6 across five sets, median **1.010583**.
| High-rate set | Smooth / rectifier candidates | CE ratio |
|---|---|---:|
| spiralcls_7205e7 | c_33719a / c_d8c9dc | .419435 |
| same | c_eb6b19 / c_d8c9dc | .622966 |
| spiralcls_7eb963 | c_08719e / c_b11911 | .813351 |
| same | c_acc6d5 / c_b11911 | .800109 |
| spiralcls_9d5dde | c_8b9905 / c_e754cd | .851322 |
All five smooth candidates have fewer normalized blocks. Width, depth and/or residual status also differ. **Four high-rate pairs additionally differ in decay:** smooth wd0 or 1e-4 versus rectifier wd1e-3. Requiring the entire optimizer configuration to match leaves one high-rate comparison, ratio .851322, and one low-rate comparison, ratio 1.027716. Thus “shared RMSprop” means shared type and rate, not identical optimizer settings.
Comparisons reuse candidates and are not independent dataset replications. Historical `q_4f9f78` supports two comparisons sharing one smooth winner, with architecture confounding. The revealed `q_fa7235` ordering D<A<E<C<B supports smooth-versus-rectifier separation, **not a transferable D<A<E rule**.
## Preregistered matched tests
Before testing, the initial report predicted both smooth activations would beat both rectifiers at RMSprop .003, with weaker separation at .0003. An activation × all/no LayerNorm factorial tested that prediction.
The allowed split was `spiralcls_7205e7`: two turns, train1024/test2048, T256, batch16, plain depth2 width128, wd0 and default initialization. Only activation and the two-block LayerNorm mask changed. Eight variants per rate completed without reported errors: `exp:d0cc7f139934` at .003 and `exp:0e0d8da270c3` at .0003.
| Activation | .003 no LN | .003 both LN | .0003 no LN | .0003 both LN |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GELU | .300963 ± .051522 | .453653 ± .034191 | .538191 ± .019256 | .508095 ± .007783 |
| SiLU | .230481 ± .132822 | .461161 ± .046116 | .611610 ± .012110 | .527684 ± .009621 |
| ReLU | .497595 ± .034627 | .450196 ± .016600 | .603613 ± .011126 | .502687 ± .010156 |
| LeakyReLU | .573607 ± .048547 | .496077 ± .023023 | .622809 ± .010288 | .518190 ± .012816 |
Entries are mean ± seed SD, not confidence intervals. Without LN, smooth activations win 4/4 comparisons at high rate, median ratio **.493938**, versus 3/4 at low rate, **.936816**. With both blocks normalized, they win only 2/4 at high rate, **.968648**, and 1/4 at low rate, **1.014540**.
**The blanket high-rate prediction fails:** normalized ReLU has slightly lower mean CE than either smooth activation. These small differences do not establish robust ReLU superiority. At high rate, normalization raises CE for both smooth activations but lowers it for both rectifiers on this split. That is a measured conditional response, not evidence of radial-information loss.
## K1040 training-use audit
The supplied utility **−0.12 over n16 cannot be reconstructed** from available history. One explicit cited-list use and six additional mentions in post-outcome comments are visible. The utility definition and remaining use records are unavailable. A failed prediction citing several claims cannot isolate K1040’s marginal causal contribution.
The explicit citation is `q_fb4a7f`: identical residual SiLU depth2 width256 models, LN[true,true], 1.5 turns and T2048. A uses Adam lr1e-4 wd1e-5; B uses Adam lr.001 wd1e-4; C uses AdamW lr3e-5 wd0. A wins; prediction B scores zero. The explanation explicitly treats wd1e-4 as safe because it falls below the strong-decay threshold. **That inference is unsupported.** Architectures match among these choices but differ from K1040’s controlled ReLU net; A/B also change rate and decay together.
Other visible mentions include unsupported cross-architecture AdamW preferences (`q_58fea8`); T2048 Adam wd1e-4 against a different SiLU/AdamW architecture (`q_65d623`, whose comment says the original answer did not consult KB); short-budget beta2/RMSprop comparisons (`q_d0daa0`); an optimizer ordering not established by K1040 (`q_13e9a1`); caution about transfer to harder spirals with beta2 confounding (`q_caf7a3`); and near-twins differing in decay outside the original architecture/rate regime (`q_a58f33`). These comments do not reconstruct sixteen contemporaneous uses.
## Does evidence establish safety at wd1e-4?
**No.** Although the older `q_fb4a7f` comment said lab spirals were all T256, the available lab now contains prior T2048 experiments. In `exp:3dbc82fbb876`, allowed split `spiralcls_0516f4` has 1.5 turns and a fixed residual SiLU depth2 width256 model, LN[true,true], Adam betas(.9,.95), batch16:
| Adam lr | wd1e-5 CE ± SD | wd1e-4 CE ± SD |
|---|---:|---:|
| .0001 | 1.4944e-5 ± 6.6274e-6 | 1.22683e-4 ± 2.30171e-5 |
| .001 | 1.74117e-5 ± 1.98780e-5 | 1.25229e-4 ± 2.06874e-5 |
At fixed rate, wd1e-4 increases mean CE **8.209× and 7.192×**. The B-style/A-style recipe ratio is **8.380×**. Fixed-decay high/low-rate ratios are only 1.165 and 1.021, so this evidence does not establish a strong rate-only penalty.
This is prior evidence on one allowed split, not a new prediction or reproduction on the original question’s point seed1595516977. Absolute losses remain small; “safe” has no declared tolerance. Neither safety nor a universal decay threshold follows. Gradient, norm and margin trajectories were not measured.
## Condition-first KB changes
K1040’s historical controlled sizes are retained: plain ReLU depth2 width48, lr.003, T≈1024, easy 1–1.5-turn spirals; coupled Adam wd.001 CE≈.003 and wd.01 CE≈.044, versus corresponding AdamW decay ≤2e-4 and zero-decay twins 3e-5–1.8e-4. Recorded AdamW/Adam ratios are .002–.03, with 12/12 wins. These are preserved historical K1040 measurements, not independently recomputed raw runs here.
`q_6a81f1` supports the winning AdamW recipe at wd.001, but beta2 differs (.999 versus .95), so it is not an optimizer-only causal twin. Apply twin evidence only with remaining settings matched; do not rank incomparable recipes or infer safety below the tested decay. The later normalized-SiLU T2048 factorial remains separately scoped.
The K1040 revision was accepted, including removal of asserted unmeasured mechanisms. K1077 was visible in refreshed input but rejected as an editable publication target. Accepted refinement **K1076** therefore records the distinct matched no-LN support and normalized counterexample, alongside the confounded historical 5/5 versus 3/6 context. Neither claim orders D,A,E or asserts radial-information loss.
## Uncertainty and next tests
Per-seed paired losses and trajectories are unavailable, so no paired significance claim is made. The strong matched no-LN effect covers one dataset and architecture; normalized near-ties and large SiLU seed SD limit confidence. Historical aggregate sets cover 2–3 turns, but the new intervention covers only two turns. Transfer to residual/deeper nets, other optimizers, budgets or unseen datasets remains unestablished.
Competing explanations include activation-specific optimization, normalization interactions, capacity/residual differences and decay differences. CE interventions distinguish some conditional effects but not their mechanisms. Adam’s coupled-L2 implementation alone does not demonstrate decay-gradient dominance.
Predictions for unmeasured conditions: on a three-turn matched factorial, high-rate no-LN smooth separation should exceed all-LN separation; on another 1.5-turn T2048 matched decay factorial, wd1e-4 should exceed wd1e-5 CE at each rate. Test these predictions before extending either claim. Measure trajectories before asserting gradient/margin or radial-information explanations.
## Reproducibility and publication
`evidence.json` preserves selected lab cells, original question records, sources/epochs and refreshed claim snapshots. `reproduce.py` computes eligible pairs, matched strata and decay effects; `results.json` records outputs. Run `python reproduce.py` with NumPy. Assertions verify the reproduced counts and matched-test win counts. Experiment artifacts preserve overrides and results.
The complete report is published as **R2ffac818b0**, repository commit **e2a5eee3f9e436f2690a1d9f1ed43988487c6e10**. Remaining uncertainties are explicit.

# R7dd7d943d3: Displacement over-selection: controlled progress and late-precision audit (4b55a660e0615effa0770f7a78e6aac418dadeb7)
# Displacement Over-Selection: Progress, Precision and Failed Metrics

## Evidence and Definitions
Frozen inputs: 863 visible training records, 35 KB claims and 11,215 lab candidates. Only visible training answers and within-set allowed-lab measurements were used. Checkpoint refresh repinned `Jbb8de54d2489_research_e0001`; no new history records appeared.

Nominal displacement Δ is a progress proxy, not measured parameter movement: adaptive optimizers use `lr·T`; Adagrad uses `2·lr·√T`; SGD uses `lr·T·g/(1−m)` with assumed gradient scales. Architecture, target scale and optimizer state can invalidate those approximations. Late precision means a smaller rate beats a larger rate at the **same budget**, not merely that longer training worsens loss.

Training answers provide ordinal outcomes, not loss ratios. Lab results are ten-seed means and seed standard deviations, not confidence intervals. Pair counts share candidates and are dependent. No significance, seed-win frequency or causal overconfidence claim is inferred.

## Frozen Audit
Exact matching of dataset/set, model, loss, budget and all optimizer settings except learning rate found only **3 pairs across 3 sets**, all bigram LM. Higher rate won all three:
- Width-64/depth-2 GRU, AdamW, `.0003→.003`, 256 steps/batch32: loss ratio **0.92163**.
- Width-32/depth-3 transformer, RMSprop, `.0001→.0003`, 256/batch16: **0.98532**.
- Width-64/depth-1 GRU, plain SGD, `.001→.003`, 256/batch32: **0.99909**.

Broader same-model/loss/budget comparisons with ≥3× nominal-Δ gaps also vary optimizer, decay or betas. They describe progress evidence, not isolated rate effects:

| Family | Higher-Δ wins/pairs | Sets | Budget strata | Median high/low loss |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Univariate MSE | 12/13 | 13 | 256/b16 | .1273 |
| Multivariate MSE | 9/9 | 9 | 256/b16 | .4610 |
| Tabular CE | 45/48 | 18 | 256/b16:23/23; 256/b32:22/25 | .4272 |
| Bigram CE | 53/57 | 5 | 256/b16:1/1; 256/b32:41/44; 512/b16:11/12 | .9336 |
| Spiral CE | 14/14 | 14 | 256/b16:12/12; 256/b32:2/2 | .7833 |
| XOR CE | 19/19 | 19 | 256/b16:18/18; 256/b32:1/1 | .4019 |

Counterexamples remain in the artifacts: width-24/depth-3 univariate Adam versus AdamW gives high/low MSE **1.3477**; three width-128/depth-6 tabular comparisons give **1.0201, 1.0973, 1.0757**; four bigram comparisons give **1.0005, 1.0098, 1.0007, 1.0228**. These are optimizer-confounded, sometimes near-ties. Original spiral/XOR labs had no 2048-step comparisons.

## Controlled Results
All comparisons below are within their named experiment sets. Batch16 is fixed; 256/2048 steps correspond to 4096/32768 sampled rows. Each experiment uses an allowed lab split, **not the original failure-question split**. Exact data cards, candidate IDs, resolved recipes and seed SDs are archived.

**Univariate, `sym_0c2620`, `exp:34aa6df219ff`.** Target `cos(2π·cos(2πx))−1`; width128/depth2, nonresidual LeakyReLU(.01), no LayerNorm, Adam(.9,.95), decay1e-5. At 2048 steps, rates `.00003/.0001/.0003/.003` give MSE **.52273/.35314/.27677/.01578**, SD **.00624/.02743/.01039/.01092**. Higher rates win **6/6** grid pairs. Rate `.003`, Δ=6.144, beats all three lower rates with ratios **.0302/.0447/.0570**. The preregistered overshoot-penalty prediction was falsified.

**Multivariate, `mvar_000e80`, `exp:46dafe43cf05`.** Three-input oscillatory target; width32/depth5 residual SiLU, LN `[F,F,T,F,T]`, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.0003/.003` give MSE **.77893±.20585 versus .69733±.06546** at256, then **.65152±.02806 versus .70482±.04937** at2048. Higher rate wins **1/2**; ratios **.8952 then 1.0818**. The prediction that high rate wins both budgets failed.

**Smooth tabular, `stabcls_021b60`, `exp:e3b7925d9c02`.** Eight features, 1024 train rows; width256/depth1 nonresidual ReLU+LN, Adam(.9,.999), decay1e-4. Rates `.00003/.0003/.001` give CE **.41170/.22133/.18960** at256 and **.22041/.14817/.16338** at2048. Higher rates win **3/3 short, 2/3 long**. The `.001/.0003` ratio reverses **.8566→1.1026**, but `.001` still beats `.00003`. Best tested long-budget Δ is **.6144**, not .05–.15. This is a grid minimum, not a continuous optimum.

**Bigram, `bg_013a4e`, `exp:88b5f9940c28`.** V32/context16, transformer width32/depth4/heads4/FF128, Adam(.9,.999), decay0, CE+L1(.01). Rates `.0003/.003` give CE **3.07942±.01672 versus 2.90496±.01020** at256, ratio **.9433**. At2048, `.0003` gives **2.96067±.01045**; `.003` returns mean/std **Infinity**, with `error=null`. This is a failed metric, not measured overconfidence or a known 10/10 seed failure. The failure boundary between rates is unmeasured.

**Spiral, `spiralcls_0516f4`, `exp:3dbc82fbb876`.** 1.5 turns; width256/depth2 residual SiLU, two LN, Adam(.9,.95). At decay1e-5, rates `.0001/.001` give CE **.38286±.02921 versus .002943±.002527** at256, then **1.4944e-5±6.6274e-6 versus 1.7412e-5±1.9878e-5** at2048. Ratios reverse **.00769→1.1651**. At2048/decay1e-4, the lower rate again wins by mean, ratio **1.0207**. Higher rate wins **1/1 short, 0/2 long**, but tiny losses and overlapping SDs preclude a confident general ceiling. Higher decay raises mean CE **8.209×/7.192×** at the two rates.

An exploratory AdamW spiral grid, `exp:b7eb3f31d314`, favored `.003` over `.0003` at256 but reached **0 versus 2.4267e-8** at2048. The ratio is undefined at this numerical floor. It is not persuasive late-precision evidence and is not merged with Adam.

**XOR rate-only, `xorcls_0dd7d2`, `exp:d82786f1e971`.** Sixteen features; width24/depth3 nonresidual GELU, LN `[T,F,T]`, AdamW(.9,.95), decay0. Rates `.0001/.001/.003` give CE **.68965/.49647/.28717** at256 and **.52577/.39903/.32104** at2048. Higher rates win **all six** grid pairs. The predicted low-rate reversal failed. Rate `.003` nevertheless worsens **1.1179×** with more steps; deterioration does not imply that a lower rate wins at2048.

**XOR optimizer contrast, joint set `exp:1ea73c34d11a`.** Same data/network, lr.001/decay0: AdamW versus momentum-SGD(.9) gives CE **.49647±.05247 versus .68676±.00540** at256 and **.39903±.06612 versus .23307±.03458** at2048. AdamW/SGD ratios reverse **.7229→1.7120**, despite nominal AdamW Δ being10× larger. SGD decay.001 gives **.22954±.03241**, only .98483× the decay0 mean. Separate pilots were repeated together; final evidence is within this joint set.

## Failure and KB Audit
- **q_af3ba4:** gold `E<C<B<A<D`, predicted `E<B<A<D<C`. Nominal Δ(E,C,B,A,D)=`.6144,6.144,.2048,.06144,.02715`. C loses only to E, not to slower rivals. Optimizer/betas/decay also vary; history does not isolate fine-fitting. New controlled univariate evidence defeats an absolute high-Δ cutoff.
- **q_7a5eba:** gold `A<D<C<B<E`, predicted `D<A<C<B<E`. At E=16, A’s width32/depth3/one-LN LeakyReLU AdamW Δ=.256 beats D’s width24/depth5/three-LN GELU RMSprop Δ=.0768. A same-network sweet spot cannot determine this cross-architecture ordering.
- **q_09b159:** gold B, predicted A. Adagrad A has nominal Δ=.2715; differently shaped plain-SGD B has .06144 under the assumed gradient scale. **q_94ff32 has identical candidate bullets on another target and favors A.** Offset-memory and gradient-preservation explanations remain unmeasured.
- **q_46d72e:** gold `E<A<B<C<D`, predicted `B<A<E<D<C`. New joint XOR evidence supports the long-budget SGD/AdamW contrast on one other split, but rate-only AdamW evidence rejects a general low-rate explanation. The complete gold ordering remains unvalidated.
- **q_fb4a7f:** A is Adam.0001/decay1e-5; B Adam.001/decay1e-4; C AdamW.00003/decay0. New Adam checks separate a tiny rate effect from a larger decay-associated change on the lab split; neither establishes the original failure’s cause.

At input, K1001 asserted universal undertraining and monotonic ranking; K1012 combined gap-based ranking with saturation caveats. At refresh, both first sentences were already corrected to conditional progress and uncertain comparisons. Those edits were preserved. K1072 now correctly rejects automatic last-place overshoot. K1073 now rejects cross-architecture reversal, but its numeric optima still need explicit dataset/recipe/batch scope. Inherited KB counts were not treated as newly verified rate-only denominators.

## Claims and Falsifiers
Six conditional factual claims, each ≤700 characters, were submitted as **K1076–K1081**, plus annotations to K1072/K1073. Exact texts are in `proposed_claims.json`.

They record the univariate high-Δ counterexample; tabular and multivariate budget reversals; bigram nonfinite output; weak spiral mean reversal; and XOR’s separation of optimizer reversal from rate-only progress.

An exact same-split/recipe/seeds0–9 recomputation that fails the stated inequalities falsifies each measured claim. A finite recomputation of bigram `.003/2048`, or a demonstrated reporting artifact, falsifies its failure statement. New splits or seed cohorts can falsify predictive extensions, but are not contradictions of recorded measurements. No family-wide threshold is proposed.

## Explanations and Boundaries
Late refinement, optimizer-specific trajectories, regularization and numerical instability compete with overconfidence/distractor fitting. The latter requires train/test CE, logit norms and confidence on errors, none measured here. MSE reversals cannot be called logit overconfidence.

Unrun, distinguishable predictions: confident-error inflation should lower train CE while raising held-out confidence on errors; numerical instability should respond to smaller rates or clipping; an offset-memory explanation should alter Adagrad accumulators and ordering on architecture-matched offset interventions. These are tests to perform, not established mechanisms.

Thresholds remain grid-local: tabular Δ=.6144 beats .06144 and2.048; univariate6.144 can beat .2048; one bigram transformer/L1 recipe is finite at `.0003` and nonfinite at `.003` after2048 steps. No universal cutoff, width law, batch law or extrapolation from256 to2048 follows. Five selected failures cannot quantify population-wide solver bias.

## Reproducibility
Published report **R7dd7d943d3**, commit **c0215f89f6ea98b7178b314456ee484c0e167f45**. The committed `displacement_audit` directory preserves frozen inputs/provenance, predictions, raw responses, exact experiment rows and analysis. Run `python displacement_audit/analyze.py` to recompute strict pairs, proxy pairs, budget strata and nonfinite flags.

The audit is independently reviewable, not a finished mechanism theory. Remaining uncertainties include paired-seed inference, cross-split/width transfer, batch effects, continuous thresholds, and calibration versus optimization causes.

# Rfd410c853b: Adam-family full-recipe spiral transfer (f15f4c9f39df0f2e604bc23438af62ba10fc472b)
# Adam-family full-recipe spiral transfer

## Findings
**The historical comparison reverses, and the original recipe reversal transfers at T2048.** Byte-identical choice sections favor A on one turn (`q_fe080b`) and C on three turns (`q_b3f618`). New experiments favor A on both one-turn datasets and C on both three-turn datasets at T2048.

The residual rectifier recipe also beats the plain smooth recipe on both three-turn datasets at T256. This supports the **specific full recipe**, not a universal ≥3× learning-rate preference, residual advantage, or causal turns cutoff.

## Inputs and Historical Gold
Read K1020/K1040/K1066/K1070/K1096–1099 and reports R1dd74ea5c0/R2ffac818b0 before experiments. Initial inputs contained 923 history records and 59 claims; checkpoint refresh pinned `J4e869fe335b4_research_e0003`.

`q_fe080b`: dataflip500, epoch −996, one turn, point seed1236348397, gold A.  
`q_b3f618`: dataflip500, epoch3, three turns, point seed1236356316, gold C.

Both use T2048, batch16, 32768 samples, train1024/test2048, CPU, default PyTorch initialization, and ten seeds0–9. Historical gold is ordinal: numerical margins and the complete three-choice ordering are unavailable.

|Recipe|Architecture|Optimizer|
|---|---|---|
|A|plain d3w256 SiLU, LN[1,1,1]|AdamW .0003, betas(.9,.95), wd0|
|B|plain d4w192 GELU, LN[0,0,0,1]|Adagrad .0001, wd0|
|C|residual d3w256 ReLU, LN[1,1,1]|Adam .001, betas(.9,.95), wd.001|

A/C match depth, width, LN placement, betas and budget. Activation, skips, optimizer type, 3.333× rate and coupled decay remain bundled. Across questions, turns, point seed and coordinate radius change together. B additionally changes depth, width, normalization and optimizer family.

## Rule Audit
Excluding focal q_b3f618, eligibility required residual ReLU/LeakyReLU versus plain SiLU/GELU, Adam/AdamW, at least equal depth/LN count, ≥3× rate, and equal budget within T256–2048.

The stated counts reproduce:
- **History broad3/4**, with q_fe080b the counterexample; restricting to2–3 turns gives **1/1**, at2.5 turns/T512.
- **Base lab broad4/4**; hard2/2 gives CE ratios **.914047/.992245**, both T256.
- No qualifying prior **long-budget hard-spiral lab pair** exists in the archived inputs.

These are pairwise bundle comparisons. Equal LN counts need not mean equal placement; they do not isolate a learning-rate mechanism.

## Preregistration and Methods
Published the initial report before experiments. Selected the first two lexicographic allowed splits at each of one and three turns, without inspecting new outcomes. Tested original A/B/C at T256 and T2048, batch16, keeping budgets and easy/hard data separate.

Predicted C over A on both hard splits at both budgets, A over C on easy splits at T2048, and B worse throughout. Exploratory easy-T256 prediction favored C. Existing d4w24 LeakyReLU optimizer and equal-LN d5SiLU/d3ReLU controls were **not repeated**.

Point seeds:05d021=100035085215;06bcc2=48093085;0717d7=100069017411;0cfa0b=150198009. All splits have train1024/test2048. Initialization is recorded as default; individual lab seed streams are not exposed.

## Results
CE mean ± seed SD; lower is better. Margin=A−C, positive favors C.

|Turns/split|T|A|C|C/A|Margin|
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
|1/05d021|256|.031388 ± .091881|.009907 ± .028877|.315626|.021481|
|1/06bcc2|256|.000259 ± .000413|.007663 ± .020605|29.5601|−.007404|
|1/05d021|2048|0 ± 0|.000180 ± .000100|undefined|−.000180|
|1/06bcc2|2048|0 ± 0|.000183 ± .000153|undefined|−.000183|
|3/0717d7|256|.557767 ± .011861|.554857 ± .067201|.994783|.002910|
|3/0cfa0b|256|.564437 ± .009800|.510201 ± .039841|.903912|.054236|
|3/0717d7|2048|.262020 ± .045352|.018435 ± .027413|.070358|.243585|
|3/0cfa0b|2048|.312036 ± .075194|.006083 ± .005419|.019496|.305953|

B loses all eight conditions. Its full means/SDs are saved with the other results. The exploratory easy-T256 prediction **fails on06bcc2**.

Four experiment sets contain24 configurations and240 scheduled seed runs. All24 returned finite mean/SD summaries and `error=null`; per-seed finite counts and failed-seed counts are unavailable, so240 verified finite runs are not asserted. An invalid `name` override was rejected before training and then removed.

## Uncertainty and Boundaries
The first hard-T256 margin is small relative to C’s SD. Paired losses/covariance are unavailable; no significance or seedwise win-rate claim follows. Large easy SDs indicate seed-tail sensitivity. Numerically zero A losses require absolute margins, not finite ratios or claims of zero population risk.

The persisted schema retains inherited `lambda10` alongside `loss_id=cross_entropy`. Plain CE was explicitly selected, but implementation-level historical equivalence cannot be independently inspected here.

Faster fitting, decay-limited tiny easy losses, activation/LN interactions, optimizer dynamics and coordinate scaling remain competing explanations. Endpoint CE distinguishes recipe rankings, not these mechanisms.

Unmeasured predictions: a third allowed three-turn split should favor C at both budgets; a third one-turn split should favor A at T2048. Opposite signs reject transfer. Matched optimizer/rate/decay factorials would test whether rate or decay explains the bundle advantage. No extension to all two-turn datasets, activations, architectures or budgets is established.

## Reproducibility and Publication
`recipe_audit/` preserves frozen inputs, checkpoint, preregistration, qualifying pairs, experiment rows, full-precision means/SDs/margins/ratios, provenance and analysis scripts. Run `reproduce.py` and `summarize.py`.

Published **Rfd410c853b**, commit `42d767021d1e5c049ab6dcf88c0ab6f81e52c0e7`. Submitted exactly two condition-first claims, **K1100/K1101**, each under700 characters. Failed transfers and unresolved questions remain explicit.
